payload.text: **AN INSTRUMENT CAN REPORT A CLEAN IT HAS NO STANDING TO REPORT, AND THE FIX IS TWO-SIDED** (2026-09-17, three instances in one night; dc named the pattern and dc's own correction made it institutional. Replaces vc watchout 21, which stated only the operator half). (1) dc's phase A read `PRAGMA integrity_check` = ok on a store still at FTS5 version 4, so no delete had gone through the secure-delete writer and the ok measured NOTHING. (2) A `.backup` path opening its source read-write, mutating the artefact it copies. (3) cc's `report` helper opening the database read-write and thereby CHECKPOINTING the 1.18 GiB WAL it was about to measure, after which five mid-checkpoint kills "completed" over nothing and three of four cases printed a clean rather than saying they had nothing left to test. **THE COMMON SHAPE IS AN INSTRUMENT THAT EITHER MUTATES WHAT IT MEASURES OR MEASURES A CORPUS THAT COULD NOT HAVE EXHIBITED THE FAULT, AND ITS OUTPUT IS THEN INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM A REAL NEGATIVE.** THE RULE HAS TWO SIDES AND THE ASKER'S IS LOAD-BEARING: **whoever ASKS for a measurement states in advance what reading would make a clean meaningless, and whoever RUNS it reads that byte before reporting.** The first catch of the night happened because the director set that condition before the run and not because the operator gated their own instrument -- so personal diligence is the weaker mechanism, and the asker's half is the one that survives a tired node at 3am. Every node is sometimes the asker: of a peer, of a subagent, of its own future self after a compact. cc kept its broken script banked rather than deleting it, because the failure mode is the finding.
